sketches.mechanism: Ownership transfer (move semantics) — after giving a value to someone else, the original binding can no longer use it
sketches.resonance: When you truly give yourself to someone, you are no longer your own; the compiler enforces this irreversibility.

sketches.mechanism: weak references — a weak var automatically becomes nil when the referenced object is deallocated, requiring optional unwrapping
sketches.resonance: Some bonds refuse to hold on; they watch the other disappear and accept the absence without crashing.

sketches.mechanism: A final variable must be assigned exactly once — the compiler forbids reassignment and forbids leaving it empty
sketches.resonance: Some things can only be decided once; the language will not let you change your mind, nor let you avoid choosing.
